To: Renters Board / Notices
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: IMPORTANT - stop using Brightline Pro 6% from batch LX2291 (check the BASE of the bottle)

Hi everyone

Short version: some of the Brightline Pro 6% (20 vol) developer we've been buying off the Kelvin Trade rep is not 6%. Part of that batch is actually 12% (40 vol). If a client reacts in your chair, it could well be this.

Kelvin Trade sent a notice yesterday. Their manufacturer had a filling error and it's affecting one batch. Here's what they say and what we need to do about it.

WHICH BATCH

- The batch code is LX2291.
- IMPORTANT: that code is printed on the BASE of the bottle. The box has no batch code on it at all. If you're checking the box you're checking the wrong thing, so check the bottle itself.
- This batch was supplied between 19 October and 5 November 2026. Any other batch, and any other strength, is not affected.
- Not every bottle in the batch is affected and you can't tell by looking at it - the colour looks the same, so don't assume yours is fine just because one of yours was fine. If in doubt, treat it as suspect.

WHAT IT DOES IF YOU USE IT

- 12% lifts much faster and much harder than 6% does.
- Signs it's too hot: foils or hair roasting, client saying it burns or is really sore at the scalp, lift going way past where it should be. A regrowth that normally takes 35-40 minutes can go pale in under 20.
- It can burn the scalp. This is a real risk, not just a bad lift.
- It also over-lifts and can leave hair brassy, patchy or blown out, and it's harder to correct afterwards.

CHECK YOUR STOCK

- Check every open bottle in your trolley as well as the stock in the back. Open and unopened.
- Check the base of each bottle.
- This is the 1L Brightline Pro 6% (20 vol) only.
- If you're not sure, send it back and ask.

WHAT TO DO WITH THE BOTTLES

- Do NOT bin them. Hold on to them and get them credited.
- The Kelvin Trade rep is in on Tuesday - hand the bottles back to him then, or take them to the Hillington depot. Either is fine, whichever's easier for you. He's giving a full credit either way.
- Send him a note of how many bottles and which batch, so he can log it.
- If a bottle caused a problem, keep that bottle and the box as well. Don't throw it out. Also keep a note of the date, the client's details, what was used and what happened.

IF SOMEONE REACTS IN THE CHAIR

- Get them to the sink straight away and rinse the affected area with plenty of cool or lukewarm running water for about an hour. Not hot water, it makes the burn worse.
- No shampoo, no creams, no oils, no other chemicals on it.
- Gloves on when you rinse, and take off any contaminated clothing if you can.
- Call 999 for medical help immediately if there's blistering, severe pain, breathing difficulty, throat swelling or collapse. Do not wait for it to get worse, and do not wait for blistering. NHS guidance for suspected chemical burns: https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/acid-and-chemical-burns/
- Chemical burns need hospital assessment. If someone's still sore or the skin looks angry after a couple of days, tell them to get it looked at.
- Write it up in the incident book at the desk while it's fresh - date, time, product, batch, how long it was on for, what the client said, what you did. Take dated photos if you can.
- Our patch test rule still stands as well: 48 hours before any colour for new clients and for anyone who hasn't had colour in 6 months. Date it on their card. Test kits are in the back cupboard, top shelf.

Aileen had the same thing on Thursday, her foils were roasting and she thought it was the heater. Lorna's had bottles off him as well, so this isn't just my stock. I'm putting this up so nobody else gets caught out - one of my clients had a reaction with this batch and it wasn't a nice one.

Kelvin Trade's email says "we apologise for any inconvenience caused". I'll leave that one there.

Questions to me or to the rep.

Kirsty
